Title: Improved asthma control with budesonide/formoterol in a single inhaler, compared with budesonide alone
Author: Zetterström et al.
Comment: The paper did not report a combined moderate-or-severe exacerbation count or a risk ratio for severe exacerbations. Severe-only participant counts were extracted. The study definition of severe exacerbation included PEF <70% of run-in mean on two consecutive days, which does not necessarily require systemic corticosteroids, an emergency visit, or hospitalization. No inferential treatment comparison was reported because event counts were too low.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Single-inhaler budesonide/formoterol (Symbicort Turbuhaler) 160/4.5 µg, two inhalations twice daily') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, parallel-group trial
Country: Finland, Germany, Ireland, Norway, Spain and Sweden
Participant type: Adults with asthma not controlled by inhaled glucocorticosteroids alone
Outcome measurement: At least one severe asthma exacerbation during 12 weeks. The paper defined severe exacerbations as need for oral steroids, discontinuation due to worsening asthma, or PEF below 70% of the run-in mean on two consecutive days.
additional_group_ns: Separate-inhaler budesonide plus formoterol: n=115; 11 patients (9.6%) had severe exacerbations; excluded because the synthesis requires ICS/LABA in one inhaler.
outcome_family: participants with at least one moderate or severe asthma exacerbation
effect_direction: Risk ratio below 1 favors medium-dose ICS plus LABA in one inhaler over the same medium-dose ICS alone.

Title: Efficacy and safety of fluticasone/formoterol combination therapy in patients with moderate-to-severe asthma
Author: Corren et al.
Comment: The reported odds ratio is presented for fluticasone/formoterol versus the comparator but is numerically oriented as comparator relative to fluticasone/formoterol (OR 1.24). Do not treat it as the planned RR. Use the raw event counts to calculate the synthesis RR oriented ICS/LABA versus ICS alone. The endpoint was tertiary and p-values were not controlled for multiple testing.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Fluticasone/formoterol 250/10 μg b.i.d.') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: 12-week double-blind randomized parallel-group phase III controlled trial
Study Environment: 78 multicentre clinical sites in North America and Europe
Medium: Single-inhaler aerosol therapy via HFA pMDI
Participant type: Adolescents and adults aged 12 years and over with moderate-to-severe asthma
Recruitment source: 78 centres in North America and Europe
Outcome measurement: Number of full-analysis-set participants with at least one treatment-emergent severe asthma exacerbation
additional_group_ns: Placebo b.i.d.: N=105; Formoterol 10 μg b.i.d.: N=110
outcome_family: participants with at least one moderate or severe asthma exacerbation
effect_direction: Risk ratio below 1 favors medium-dose ICS plus LABA in one inhaler over the same medium-dose ICS alone.

Report_ID: Number of patients experiencing ≥1 on-treatment severe asthma exacerbation
Title: Once-daily fluticasone furoate (FF)/vilanterol reduces risk of severe exacerbations in asthma versus FF alone
Author: Eric D Bateman et al.
Comment: The hazard ratio is the paper’s related time-to-first-event estimate and is not a risk ratio. For the planned meta-analysis, calculate the risk ratio from the directly reported ITT participant counts (FF/VI 154/1009 versus FF 186/1010). The paper reports severe exacerbations only, not a combined moderate-or-severe outcome. The study began on 22 February 2010 and ended on 15 September 2011; study_year records the explicitly stated start year.
Design Type: Phase III randomized, multicentre, double-blind, parallel-group, event-driven controlled trial
domain: Asthma treatment and severe exacerbation prevention
Medium: Single ELLIPTA dry powder inhaler; once-daily evening treatment
Participant type: Adolescents and adults aged ≥12 years with asthma uncontrolled on ICS or ICS/LABA and at least one exacerbation in the prior year
Outcome measurement: At least one adjudicated on-treatment severe asthma exacerbation; severe exacerbations required systemic corticosteroids for at least 3 days, inpatient hospitalization, or an emergency department visit due to asthma requiring systemic corticosteroids.
Outcome variable: Number of patients experiencing ≥1 on-treatment severe asthma exacerbation
outcome_family: participants with at least one moderate or severe asthma exacerbation
effect_direction: Risk ratio below 1 favors medium-dose ICS plus LABA in one inhaler over the same medium-dose ICS alone.

Report_ID: Participants experiencing at least one severe asthma exacerbation over 12 weeks
Title: Budesonide/formoterol fumarate dihydrate versus budesonide with a novel suspension technology for uncontrolled asthma: phase 3 LITHOS study
Author: Papi et al.
Comment: Severe-exacerbation counts only; no combined moderate-or-severe participant counts were reported. The paper explicitly describes both the study regimens and qualifying prior treatment as low-dose, whereas the synthesis contract specifies medium-dose therapy, so dose-based eligibility requires reviewer adjudication and this row may ultimately be excluded. Denominators are the final analysed efficacy set from Table 3, not the 374 randomised or 353 treated participants. The separately reported 0.48 (95% CI 0.23–0.97) is a negative-binomial exacerbation rate ratio based on recurrent events and follow-up time, not the participant-level risk ratio requested, so it was not entered as an RR.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('BFFA 160: budesonide/formoterol fumarate dihydrate 160/10 μg via Aerosphere MDI twice daily') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); excluded by outcome classification: does not match the requested outcome/timepoint (meta_analysis_candidate=False)
Design Type: 12-week phase 3 randomised double-blind parallel-group multicentre superiority trial
Country: Canada; Czechia; Republic of Korea; Malaysia; Philippines; South Africa; USA
Participant type: Participants aged 12–80 years with inadequately controlled asthma despite low-dose ICS or ICS/LABA
Recruitment source: 106 clinical study sites across seven countries
Outcome measurement: Number of efficacy-set participants experiencing at least one severe asthma exacerbation during 12 weeks
Outcome variable: Participants experiencing at least one severe asthma exacerbation over 12 weeks
outcome_family: participants with at least one moderate or severe asthma exacerbation
effect_direction: Risk ratio below 1 favors ICS plus LABA in one inhaler over the same ICS alone.
